short.title: Finding Facts vs. Connecting Dots
short.text:
Your students can find any fact in seconds. Can they connect the dots? 🔗

In The Future Ready Challenge I wrote: "Possessing the information and being able to connect the dots are two very different things."

So the job isn't handing them answers. It's teaching them to think.

That's why I built VIC to work as a co-teacher that asks students questions instead of handing out answers. You see what they worked on, and every decision stays with you.

Free for teachers: askvic.ai (link in bio)

linkedin_optional.text:
Before I was a principal, I was a principal's kid.

My dad used to bribe my friends with lunch to come help at his school. I didn't know it was a management tactic. For the price of lunch, he got a lot of work out of them.

He had a saying: "Kiss your ducks in the morning, your day is bound to get better." Don't let the rough things hang over you. Get them done and get them behind you.

And he was a farmer's kid. Plowing the garden, he taught me that if you watch your feet, the line comes out crooked. Look way out to where you're aiming, and it comes out straight.

Feed your people. Do the hard thing first. Keep your eyes on the goal.

What did a parent or mentor teach you about leading before you knew you were learning it?

short.title: Principals: What Would You Do?
short.text:
Principals and teachers: what would you do? 🤔

A parent sends back the board-approved, attorney-written field-trip form with handwritten changes. Her edits say the school can't use it to escape responsibility if her child gets hurt.

You explain that the school is responsible for her child on the trip either way. She still won't sign a clean copy.

Keep arguing, keep the child home, or find out what the law actually requires? Comment your call. What I chose is in the first comment.

This is one of 12 real scenarios in my What Would You Do? 12 School Leadership Scenarios deck, each with what I actually chose. Link in bio.

#principal #principallife #schoolleadership #teachersoftiktok #teachersofinstagram #fieldtrip
short.first_comment:
What I chose: I asked her to sign a clean copy, and she refused. So I called our school attorney, who confirmed her edits did not change the school's responsibility. We said okay and took her child on the trip. We were not going to make a child lose an experience over an argument that had no legal impact.

Know the law. Lower the temperature. Keep the child at the center.
